mainTopic: How much of קריאת שמע requires כוונה, and practical rules for saying it: stretching אחד, standing still, the first פסוק alone, body position, and greeting others during שמע
overview: This amud asks how much of קריאת שמע needs כוונה, and then looks at several practical rules for saying it. רבי עקיבא learns from 'על לבבך' that the whole first פרשה needs כוונה, and רבי יוחנן rules like him. A second version attaches the ruling to רבי אחא instead, with the same practical result. Another ברייתא brings the dispute between רב זוטרא and רבי יאשיה about where כוונה and קריאה apply, and the גמרא explains both views. רבי מאיר says only the first פסוק needs כוונה, and רבא rules like him. The גמרא then teaches how to stretch the word אחד, which part of שמע must be said standing still, and that רבי יהודה הנשיא said only the first פסוק during his lesson. It also rules that saying the first פסוק before falling asleep is enough, and that one may not say שמע lying on one's back. Finally, it returns to the משנה about greeting people during שמע and corrects its wording to show how רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה differ. That corrected text continues on the next amud.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא: the whole paragraph needs intent
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא rejects רבי אליעזר's limit. He reads 'אשר אנכי מצוך היום על לבבך' as teaching that the entire פרשה requires כוונה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says: 'Which I command you this day, upon your heart.' From here you learn that the entire paragraph requires focused intent.
steps.whatsHappening: We are in the middle of a ברייתא. רבי עקיבא is answering רבי אליעזר, who had said only the first part of שמע needs כוונה. רבי עקיבא uses a different phrase in the פסוק to prove that the whole paragraph needs כוונה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר read the word 'האלה' (these) as a limit: only 'these' opening words need כוונה. רבי עקיבא points to the very next words, 'אשר אנכי מצוך היום על לבבך'. 'Upon your heart' refers to everything 'I command you', so the requirement of focused intent stretches over the whole פרשה.

keyTerms.meaning: Focused intent; concentrating the heart on what one is saying
A paragraph or section of the Torah (here, the first paragraph of שמע)
From here you learn (introduces a derivation from a verse)
Upon your heart

steps.confusionAlert: 'כל הפרשה כולה' here means the whole first paragraph (שמע / ואהבת). It does not mean all three paragraphs of קריאת שמע.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן rules like רבי עקיבא
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר בר חנה reports in the name of רבי יוחנן that the הלכה follows רבי עקיבא: the whole first paragraph needs כוונה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר בר חנה said in the name of רבי יוחנן: the law follows רבי עקיבא.
steps.whatsHappening: After the dispute, an אמורא gives the practical ruling. The הלכה is like רבי עקיבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This settles the ברייתא's argument in practice. One must have כוונה for the entire first פרשה of שמע, not just the opening פסוק or words.

steps.title: Second version: the תוספתא about כוונה in שמע
steps.stepSummary: Some attach רבי יוחנן's ruling to a different תוספתא. There the תנא קמא requires כוונה for שמע, and רבי אחא in the name of רבי יהודה says כוונה in the first פרק is enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some teach this ruling on a different source, which was taught: one who reads שמע must focus his heart. רבי אחא in the name of רבי יהודה says: once he focused his heart in the first section, he no longer needs to.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers an alternate tradition of where רבי יוחנן's ruling was said. It first quotes the source text, which sets up the ruling in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this version the dispute is between a תנא קמא, who seems to require כוונה for the whole of שמע, and רבי אחא, who limits it to the first פרק. The ruling attached to this source comes in the next step.

The first section (the first paragraph of שמע)

steps.title: In the second version, the ruling follows רבי אחא
steps.stepSummary: In this version, רבי יוחנן rules like רבי אחא in the name of רבי יהודה: only the first פרק needs כוונה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר בר חנה said in the name of רבי יוחנן: the law follows רבי אחא, who spoke in the name of רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: This finishes the alternate version. רבי יוחנן's ruling is that כוונה is required only for the first section.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The wording looks different from step 2, but the practical result is the same. רבי עקיבא required כוונה for the whole first paragraph. רבי אחא requires כוונה for the first פרק. Either way, the first paragraph needs כוונה and the later paragraphs do not.

steps.title: Another ברייתא: שמע may not be read out of order
steps.stepSummary: Another ברייתא learns from the word 'והיו' that שמע must not be read in reverse order.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another ברייתא taught: 'And they shall be' teaches that one may not read it out of order.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא on the same topic. Its first teaching is that the words of שמע must be said in their proper sequence.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'והיו' means 'they shall be', which the ברייתא reads as: the words must stay as they are, in their written order. Reading them backwards or rearranged does not fulfill the מצוה.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught in another ברייתא
And they shall be
Out of order; in reverse sequence

phrases.english: It was taught in another baraita:
'And they shall be': that he should not read it out of order.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Introduces a new ברייתא with further derivations about קריאת שמע.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: קריאת שמע may not be read out of order.

steps.title: רב זוטרא and רבי יאשיה disagree about כוונה and קריאה
steps.stepSummary: On 'על לבבך', רב זוטרא says the section up to here is a מצות כוונה and from here on a מצות קריאה. רבי יאשיה says the opposite.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Upon your heart': רב זוטרא says, up to here is the מצוה of intent; from here on is the מצוה of reading. רבי יאשיה says, up to here is the מצוה of reading; from here on is the מצוה of intent.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues with a dispute about the words 'על לבבך'. Two opinions mark this phrase as a dividing line between two kinds of obligation, but they reverse which kind comes first. This sets up the explanation that follows in the גמרא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רב זוטרא, 'על לבבך' (upon your heart) shows that the verses up to this point demand heart-focus, and after this only proper reading is needed. רבי יאשיה reverses the two. His view is surprising and needs explanation, which the גמרא will give next.

keyTerms.meaning: Up to here
From here onward
The obligation of focused intent
The obligation of reading aloud (properly)

steps.confusionAlert: רב זוטרא does not mean that after 'על לבבך' one may skip the words. He means one must still read them, just without the special requirement of כוונה.

phrases.english: 'Upon your heart':
Rav Zutra says:
up to here is the מצוה of intent;
from here onward is the מצוה of reading.
Rabbi Yoshiya says:
up to here is the מצוה of reading;
from here onward is the מצוה of intent.

steps.triggerLanguage: עַל לְבָבֶךָ רַב זוּטְרָא אוֹמֵר עַד כָּאן מִצְוַת כַּוָּונָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא with a second derivation, from 'על לבבך'.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב זוטרא: כוונה up to 'על לבבך', and only reading afterward. רבי יאשיה: reading up to 'על לבבך', and כוונה afterward.

steps.title: Why is only the later section a מצות קריאה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב זוטרא. If the later section is a מצות קריאה because it says 'לדבר בם', the first section also says 'ודברת בם', so it should need קריאה too.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is different that from here on there is a מצוה of reading? Is it because it is written 'to speak of them'? Here too it is written 'and you shall speak of them'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a question on רב זוטרא. At first it reads him as saying that the first section needs only thinking (כוונה) and only the later section needs saying the words (קריאה).
steps.deeperAnalysis: The source for 'reading' would be the word 'לדבר בם' (to speak of them) in the second פרשה. But the first פרשה has nearly the same words, 'ודברת בם'. So why would reading apply only to the later part?

keyTerms.meaning: What is different? The גמרא asks why two similar cases are treated differently
The מצוה of saying the words out loud
'And you shall speak of them', from the first פרשה of שמע
'To speak of them', from the second פרשה (והיה אם שמע)

steps.confusionAlert: Here 'מכאן ואילך' (from here on) means the second פרשה. The גמרא first assumes רב זוטרא meant that the first part has ONLY כוונה and NO קריאה. That assumption is exactly what is being challenged.

phrases.english: What is different that from here on

phrases.english: there is a מצוה of reading?
Because it is written: 'to speak of them'?

steps.kashyaTarget: רב זוטרא's claim that only the section after 'על לבבך' is a מצות קריאה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The verse that supposedly creates the reading requirement ('לדבר בם') has a parallel in the first פרשה ('ודברת בם'). So reading should apply there too.

steps.title: The first section needs both intent and reading
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא reinterprets רב זוטרא. Up to 'על לבבך' both כוונה and קריאה are required. From there on, only קריאה without כוונה is required.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what he means: up to here is a מצוה of intent and reading; from here on, reading without intent.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by explaining what רב זוטרא really meant. The first part is not 'intent only'. It is 'intent plus reading'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question assumed the first part had no reading requirement. The answer adds reading to the first part, so 'ודברת בם' is no longer a problem. The real difference between the parts is only about כוונה.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what he means. It introduces a re-reading of an earlier statement
Reading the words without the requirement of focused intent

phrases.aramaic: הָכִי קָאָמַר: עַד כָּאן מִצְוַת כַּוָּונָה וּקְרִיאָה,
phrases.english: This is what he is saying: up to here is a מצוה of intent and reading,
from here on, reading without intent.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 7 by re-reading רב זוטרא's words
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The first section required only כוונה, and the second only קריאה
steps.terutzMaskana: The first section requires both כוונה and קריאה. The second requires קריאה without כוונה.

steps.title: The second section also mentions the heart
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges again. If the first section needs כוונה because of 'על לבבך', the second section also says 'על לבבכם', so it should need כוונה too.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what is different that up to here is a מצוה of intent and reading, because it is written 'upon your heart… and you shall speak of them'? There too it is written 'upon your heart… to speak of them'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a new question on the answer it just gave. Why should only the first section need כוונה?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first section's two requirements come from two phrases: 'על לבבך' (heart = intent) and 'ודברת בם' (speech = reading). The second section has the same pair: 'על לבבכם' and 'לדבר בם'. So it seems it should also need both intent and reading.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Upon your heart', in the first פרשה. It is the source for כוונה
'Upon your hearts', the parallel phrase in the second פרשה
There too. It points out that the other case has the same feature

phrases.english: And what is different that up to here
there is a מצוה of intent and reading
because it is written: 'upon your heart… and you shall speak of them'?
There too it is written:
'upon your hearts… to speak of them'!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמַאי שְׁנָא עַד כָּאן מִצְוַת כַּוָּונָה וּקְרִיאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the revised understanding given in Step 8
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the second section needs קריאה without כוונה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The second פרשה contains the same 'heart' phrase that creates the כוונה requirement in the first. So it should also need כוונה.

steps.title: 'Upon your hearts' is needed for רבי יצחק's teaching on תפילין
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that 'על לבבכם' in the second פרשה is used for a different law. רבי יצחק learns from it that the arm-תפילין must be placed opposite the heart. So it does not teach כוונה.
steps.simpleTranslation: That verse is needed for what רבי יצחק said: 'And you shall place these words' teaches that the placing must be opposite the heart.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question. The heart phrase in the second פרשה is 'used up' for a different lesson, so it cannot also teach a כוונה requirement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A phrase in a פסוק that is needed to teach one law is not available to teach another. רבי יצחק reads 'ושמתם... על לבבכם' literally: the תפילין containing these words go on the arm facing the heart. That leaves only the first פרשה's 'על לבבך' as the source for כוונה.

keyTerms.meaning: It is needed for. The verse is used for a different teaching
'And you shall place', from the second פרשה
Placement opposite the heart. It refers to the arm-תפילין

steps.whatToRemember: According to רב זוטרא, the first part of שמע needs both כוונה and קריאה. The rest needs only קריאה. The second פרשה's 'על לבבכם' teaches where to put the arm-תפילין, not כוונה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains the source for the הלכה that the arm-תפילין is placed on the arm facing the heart. It also shows a common גמרא pattern: a verse needed for one teaching cannot be used for another.

phrases.aramaic: הַהוּא מִבְּעֵי לֵיהּ לְכִדְרַבִּי יִצְחָק דְּאָמַר:
phrases.english: That verse is needed for what רבי יצחק taught, who said:
'And you shall place these words of Mine'
phrases.notes: Devarim 11:18, read as referring to the פרשיות inside the תפילין

phrases.english: the placing must be opposite the heart.
phrases.notes: The arm-תפילין is positioned facing the heart

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 9
steps.terutzResolutionType: The verse is needed for another teaching (מבעי ליה)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'על לבבכם' in the second פרשה would require כוונה there
steps.terutzMaskana: 'על לבבכם' teaches that the arm-תפילין goes opposite the heart, so the second פרשה has no כוונה requirement according to רב זוטרא

steps.title: Challenging רבי יאשיה: the first section also says 'upon your heart'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי יאשיה's view and asks why only the later section needs כוונה, since the first section also says 'על לבבך'.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: רבי יאשיה says, up to here is a מצות קריאה, and from here on is a מצות כוונה. What is different about the later part that it needs כוונה? Is it because it says 'על לבבכם'? Here too, in the first part, it says 'על לבבך'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings back רבי יאשיה's opinion and attacks it. Its point is that the verse that supposedly teaches כוונה appears in both sections.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יאשיה said only the later section needs כוונה. The likely source is the words 'על לבבכם', 'upon your heart', in the second פרשה. But the first פרשה has almost the same words, 'על לבבך', so by that logic the first part should need כוונה too.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The Master said.' The גמרא uses this to quote an earlier statement so it can analyze it.
'What is different?' It asks why two similar cases are treated differently.
'Here too.' It points out that the same reason also applies to the other case.
'Upon your (plural) heart.' This is from the second פרשה of שמע.

steps.confusionAlert: This is the mirror image of steps 7–10. There, the גמרא tested רב זוטרא's view. Now it runs the same kind of test on רבי יאשיה, who holds the reverse.

phrases.english: Up to here is a מצוה of reciting,
from here on is a מצוה of intent.

phrases.english: What is different that from here on there is a מצוה of intent?
Because it is written 'upon your heart'?
Here too it is written 'upon your heart'!
phrases.notes: The first פרשה uses the same words.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי שְׁנָא מִכָּאן וְאֵילָךְ מִצְוַת כַּוָּונָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After finishing with רב זוטרא, the גמרא turns to test the second opinion, רבי יאשיה's.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יאשיה's claim that only the later section requires כוונה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The source for כוונה, 'upon your heart', appears in both sections. So it cannot explain why the sections are treated differently.

steps.title: Reinterpreting רבי יאשיה: first part needs both, later part needs intent without recitation
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that רבי יאשיה really means the first part needs both קריאה and כוונה, while the later part needs כוונה without קריאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what he means: up to here, there is a מצוה of both קריאה and כוונה. From here on, there is כוונה without קריאה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rereads רבי יאשיה's words to fit both verses. The first section does need כוונה, and on top of that it needs קריאה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now 'על לבבך' in the first section is no problem, because the first section does need כוונה too. The real difference between the sections is about קריאה. Only the first section has a Torah-level obligation of recitation.

keyTerms.meaning: 'This is what he means.' The גמרא uses it to reinterpret a statement.
'Intent without recitation.' Here the verse teaches כוונה but does not create a recitation obligation.

phrases.english: This is what he is saying:
up to here, a מצוה of reciting and intent,
from here on, intent without reciting.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 11 by reinterpreting רבי יאשיה.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought רבי יאשיה meant the first section needs only קריאה, with no כוונה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The first section needs both קריאה and כוונה. The later section needs כוונה without קריאה.

steps.title: Challenging again: the second section also says 'to speak of them'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why only the first section needs קריאה, since the second section also mentions speaking: 'לדבר בם'.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what is different that up to here there is a מצוה of קריאה and כוונה? Because it says 'על לבבך' and 'ודברת בם'? There too, in the second section, it says 'על לבבכם … לדבר בם'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the new explanation from the other side. The second section also has a phrase about speaking, so it should need קריאה too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first section needs both because it has two phrases: 'על לבבך' for כוונה and 'ודברת בם' for קריאה. But the second section also has both, 'על לבבכם' and 'לדבר בם'. So why does the second section lack the קריאה obligation?

keyTerms.meaning: 'And you shall speak of them.' This is from the first פרשה and is the source for קריאה.
'To speak of them.' This is from the second פרשה.
'There.' Here it refers to the second section.

phrases.english: And what is different that up to here
there is a מצוה of reciting and intent?
Because it is written 'upon your heart' and 'you shall speak of them'?
There too it is written
'upon your heart … to speak of them'!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמַאי שְׁנָא עַד כָּאן מִצְוַת קְרִיאָה וְכַוָּונָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reinterpretation given in step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the later section has no קריאה obligation
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Both sections contain a 'speaking' phrase. So the source for קריאה applies equally to both.

steps.title: 'To speak of them' in the second section is about teaching Torah
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that 'לדבר בם' in the second פרשה refers to Torah learning in general: teach your children Torah so they will be fluent in it.
steps.simpleTranslation: That verse is written about Torah learning. This is what the Torah is saying: teach your children Torah, so that they will be fluent in it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבי יאשיה by showing that 'לדבר בם' in the second section has a different job. It is about teaching Torah to children, not about reciting שמע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the second פרשה, 'לדבר בם' comes right after 'ולמדתם אתם את בניכם', 'and you shall teach them to your children'. So it describes the goal of teaching: that the children will speak Torah fluently. It does not create an obligation to recite this section of שמע.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Words of Torah,' meaning Torah study in general.
'The Merciful One.' A name for ה׳, used when saying what the Torah means.
'Teach your children.'
'They will be well-versed' or fluent, from גירסא.

steps.whatToRemember: The גמרא treats both opinions the same way. רב זוטרא: first section needs כוונה and קריאה, later section needs קריאה only, because 'על לבבכם' is about where the תפילין go. רבי יאשיה: first section needs קריאה and כוונה, later section needs כוונה only, because 'לדבר בם' is about teaching Torah. Each side explains away the extra verse by giving it a different job.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a common גמרא technique. When a verse seems to prove too much, the גמרא shows that the verse is already 'used up' for a different law.

phrases.english: That one is written about words of Torah.
And this is what the Merciful One is saying:
Teach your children Torah,
so that they will be well-versed in them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 13 by giving 'לדבר בם' a different meaning.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Verse assigned to a different law
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We assumed 'לדבר בם' in the second פרשה teaches an obligation to recite.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'לדבר בם' in the second פרשה teaches the duty to teach Torah to one's children until they are fluent. It does not teach recitation of שמע.

steps.title: Only the first פסוק needs כוונה according to רבי מאיר
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא records רבי מאיר's view that כוונת הלב is needed only up to the end of שמע ישראל.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: 'Hear, Israel, ה׳ is our God, ה׳ is One.' Up to here, focus of the heart is needed. These are the words of רבי מאיר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא that gives a short and clear answer to the question it has been discussing: how much of שמע needs כוונה? רבי מאיר says only the first פסוק does.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier opinions said כוונה is needed until על לבבך, or for different amounts of the two פרשיות. רבי מאיר makes the required amount much smaller. Only the single פסוק of שמע ישראל, where we accept ה׳ as King, needs real focus.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The Rabbis taught.' This phrase opens a ברייתא.
Focus or intention of the heart
Up to here
These are the words of רבי מאיר

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
'Hear, Israel, the Lord is our God, the Lord is One'
up to here, intention of the heart is required,
these are the words of Rabbi Meir.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the back-and-forth about רבי יאשיה's view, the גמרא brings another opinion that limits כוונה to the first פסוק only.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: כוונת הלב is needed only for the first פסוק, שמע ישראל.

steps.title: רבא rules that the הלכה follows רבי מאיר
steps.stepSummary: רבא rules that the הלכה follows רבי מאיר: only the first פסוק requires כוונה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: The הלכה follows רבי מאיר.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives the final ruling in הלכה for the whole כוונה discussion. We follow רבי מאיר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא brought several opinions about how far כוונה is needed. רבא settles the question in practice. One must have כוונה for the first פסוק, and the rest of שמע does not require it to be יוצא.

keyTerms.meaning: The halacha follows (this opinion)
A major אמורא whose rulings are usually followed

steps.whatToRemember: The הלכה follows רבי מאיר. Only the first פסוק, שמע ישראל, absolutely requires כוונה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for the practical הלכה that a person must focus on the meaning of the first פסוק of שמע.

phrases.english: Rava said:
The halakha is in accordance with Rabbi Meir.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the practical ruling on the ברייתא in step 15.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: In practice, כוונה is required only for the first פסוק of שמע.

steps.title: Stretching out the word אחד brings long life
steps.stepSummary: סומכוס teaches that whoever stretches out the word אחד will have his days and years lengthened.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: סומכוס says, whoever stretches out the word 'אחד' gets his days and years stretched out.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic connected to the first פסוק: how to say the word אחד. סומכוס promises a reward for saying it slowly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Stretching out אחד gives a person time to think about ה׳ being One and the only King. The reward matches the act: you lengthen אחד, so ה׳ lengthens your life.

keyTerms.meaning: 'It was taught.' This phrase introduces a ברייתא.
A תנא, a student of רבי מאיר
One who stretches out or lengthens
His days and his years

phrases.english: It was taught: Sumakhos says:
Anyone who extends the word 'One,'
they extend for him his days and years.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from how much needs כוונה to how the key word אחד in the first פסוק should be said.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Stretching out the word אחד is a good practice, and it is rewarded with long life.

steps.title: Stretch out the ד of אחד
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בר יעקב adds that the stretching should be done on the letter ד.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא בר יעקב said: And on the ד.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחא בר יעקב explains how to fulfill סומכוס's teaching. The lengthening should be on the last letter, the ד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying the ד clearly and at length lets the whole word be heard properly. It also gives the person time to think about ה׳'s rule, as the next steps describe.

keyTerms.meaning: The letter ד

phrases.english: Rav Aḥa bar Ya'akov said:
And on the dalet.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אַחָא בַּר יַעֲקֹב: וּבַדָּלֵית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains which letter סומכוס meant should be stretched.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The lengthening of אחד is done on the ד.

steps.title: Do not rush the ח
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי warns that while stretching the ד, one must not rush through the ח.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: As long as he does not rush the ח.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי adds a limit to the previous teaching. Focus on the ד, but do not swallow the ח in a hurry.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone who stretches the ד might rush the earlier letters. If the ח is rushed, the word comes out wrong. Every letter must still be said properly.

keyTerms.meaning: As long as, provided that
Grab quickly, rush through
The letter ח

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
Provided that he does not rush the ḥet.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי: וּבִלְבַד שֶׁלֹּא יַחֲטוֹף בַּחֵית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a condition to רב אחא בר יעקב's instruction.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: While stretching the ד, the ח must still be said clearly and not rushed.

steps.title: There is a limit to how long you stretch אחד
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה tells רבי חייא בר אבא, who stretched אחד very long, that once he has thought of ה׳ as King everywhere, he does not need more.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה was sitting before רבי חייא בר אבא and saw that he stretched out אחד a lot. He said to him: Once you have made Him King above, below, and in all four directions of the heavens, you do not need more.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story that sets a limit on stretching אחד. Stretch it only long enough to think that ה׳ rules everywhere.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This story explains why we stretch אחד in the first place: to think about ה׳'s rule over everything. Once that thought is complete, stretching it longer adds nothing. So the practice has a clear limit.

keyTerms.meaning: Was sitting before him
A lot, very much
You made Him King
The four directions of the heavens
You do not need any more

steps.whyThisMatters: This gives the practical measure for how long to stretch אחד: long enough to have in mind that ה׳ rules above, below, and in all four directions.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya was sitting
before Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Abba,
he saw that he was extending a lot,
he said to him:
Once you have crowned Him above and below
and in the four directions of the heavens
you do not need any more.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sets an upper limit on the lengthening of אחד described in steps 17 to 19.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Stretch אחד only long enough to have in mind that ה׳ rules everywhere. More than that is unnecessary.

steps.title: רב יהודה: על לבבך must be said standing still
steps.stepSummary: רב נתן בר מר עוקבא quotes רב יהודה: 'על לבבך' must be said בעמידה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נתן בר מר עוקבא said in the name of רב יהודה: 'על לבבך' is said while standing still.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic: which part of שמע must be said while standing still, not walking. Its wording will be questioned right away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'על לבבך' are the same marker used before for how far כוונה goes. Here רב יהודה links them to standing still, but as written his statement sounds as if only those two words need it.

keyTerms.meaning: While standing still, stopped in one place and not walking
'On your heart,' a phrase near the end of the first פסוקים of שמע

steps.confusionAlert: בעמידה here does not mean standing up instead of sitting. It means stopping in one place instead of walking, as the Sefaria translation 'standing in one place' shows.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב נָתָן בַּר מָר עוּקְבָא
phrases.english: Rav Natan bar Mar Ukva said
that Rav Yehuda said:
'Upon your heart' while standing.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נָתָן בַּר מָר עוּקְבָא אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new subject: physical position while saying שמע.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Part of שמע must be said while standing still.

steps.title: Can it really mean only those two words?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: could it really be that only the words 'על לבבך' must be said standing still?
steps.simpleTranslation: 'על לבבך'? Does that make sense?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the wording of רב יהודה's statement. It makes no sense that only the two words 'על לבבך' need standing still.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nothing about those two words sets them apart from the rest of שמע. Read literally, the statement is strange, so the wording must be wrong or incomplete.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Would it enter your mind?' It is used to reject an impossible reading.

phrases.english: 'Upon your heart' — does it enter your mind?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the literal wording of רב יהודה's statement.
steps.kashyaTarget: The wording '״על לבבך״ בעמידה' in רב יהודה's statement
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: There is no reason that only the two words על לבבך would require standing still. The literal reading is illogical.

steps.title: Correct reading: up to על לבבך standing still
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא corrects the wording: everything up to 'על לבבך' must be said standing still, and from there on it is not needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, say: Up to 'על לבבך' is said standing still. From here on, it is not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fixes רב יהודה's statement by adding the word 'עד', meaning 'until.' The whole opening section, up to על לבבך, must be said standing still.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With the word עד, the statement makes sense. It matches the earlier opinion that כוונה is needed up to על לבבך. The part that needs focus is the part said while standing still.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Rather, say.' The גמרא is correcting the text.
From here onward

phrases.english: Rather, say:
Until 'upon your heart' while standing.
From here on — not.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא by fixing the wording of the statement.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Only the words על לבבך require standing still.
steps.terutzMaskana: Everything up to and including על לבבך requires standing still. After that, one may walk.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: the whole first פרשה standing still
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן disagrees and says the entire first פרשה must be said standing still.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוחנן said: The whole פרשה is said standing still.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן gives a different opinion from רב יהודה. He requires the whole first פרשה, not just up to על לבבך, to be said standing still.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יהודה stops the requirement at על לבבך. רבי יוחנן extends it to the end of the first פרשה. The two opinions disagree only about how far the requirement goes.

keyTerms.meaning: The whole entire פרשה, here the first one

steps.whatToRemember: There are two opinions about standing still for שמע. רב יהודה says it is needed up to על לבבך. רבי יוחנן says it is needed for the whole first פרשה.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
The entire portion while standing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives an opposing opinion to the corrected statement of רב יהודה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The entire first פרשה of שמע must be said standing still.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן is consistent with his own view
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows that רבי יוחנן's view in Step 24 fits another ruling of his: the הלכה follows רבי אחא in the name of רבי יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוחנן follows his own reasoning. For רבה בר בר חנה said in the name of רבי יוחנן: the הלכה follows רבי אחא, who spoke in the name of רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that רבי יוחנן's demand to stand still for the whole first פרשה matches another ruling he gave elsewhere.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, רבי אחא in the name of רבי יהודה said that the whole first פרשה needs כוונה. רבי יוחנן rules like him. So it makes sense that he also requires standing still for that whole פרשה, since standing still helps a person concentrate.

keyTerms.meaning: He follows his own reasoning, meaning he is consistent with what he said elsewhere
The practical law follows...
In the name of

steps.confusionAlert: Here רבי יהודה is the תנא quoted by רבי אחא. He is not רבי יהודה הנשיא, who appears in the next step.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yochanan follows his own reasoning,
for Rabba bar bar Chana said
that Rabbi Yochanan said:
The law follows Rabbi Acha,
phrases.notes: רבי אחא held that the whole first פרשה requires כוונה.

phrases.english: who said it in the name of Rabbi Yehuda.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows that רבי יוחנן's view in Step 24 is consistent with another ruling of his.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוחנן rules like רבי אחא, so the whole first פרשה needs כוונה. This explains why he requires standing still for all of it.

steps.title: רבי's שמע was only the first פסוק
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that the single פסוק 'שמע ישראל' was the whole קריאת שמע of רבי יהודה הנשיא.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: 'Hear, Israel, ה׳ is our God, ה׳ is One.' This was the קריאת שמע of רבי יהודה הנשיא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that opens a new topic: רבי יהודה הנשיא said only the first פסוק of שמע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This shows that the first פסוק is the core of the מצוה. Accepting מלכות שמים is the most essential part. The next steps explain how and when רבי did this.

keyTerms.meaning: The Rabbis taught, which introduces a ברייתא
The reading of שמע
The leader of the generation and editor of the משנה, often called simply 'רבי'

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
'Hear, Israel, ה׳ is our God, ה׳ is One'
this is the reading of Shema
of Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic about the minimum of קריאת שמע.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יהודה הנשיא's קריאת שמע consisted only of the first פסוק.

steps.title: רב never saw רבי accept מלכות שמים
steps.stepSummary: רב tells רבי חייא that he never saw רבי accept מלכות שמים, meaning he never saw him say שמע.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said to רבי חייא: I never saw רבי accept upon himself מלכות שמים.
steps.whatsHappening: רב raises a puzzle: he spent time with רבי but never saw him say שמע. This sets up רבי חייא's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since a great person like רבי surely said שמע, רב wants to know when and how he did it. 'Accepting מלכות שמים' is another way of saying 'saying the first פסוק of שמע.'

keyTerms.meaning: The Kingship of Heaven, accepting ה׳ as King
I did not see

phrases.english: Rav said to Rabbi Chiya:
I did not see Rebbi
accepting upon himself the Kingship of Heaven.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks how רבי's short שמע actually took place.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: When and how did רבי accept מלכות שמים, since רב never saw it?

steps.title: רבי accepted it when passing his hands over his face
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא answers that when רבי passed his hands over his face, he was saying שמע and accepting עול מלכות שמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Son of noblemen, when רבי passes his hands over his face, he is accepting upon himself the yoke of מלכות שמים.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חייא solves רב's puzzle: רבי said שמע quietly, covering his eyes in the middle of his teaching.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי did not stop his lesson in an obvious way. He covered his face, said the one פסוק, and continued. That is why רב never noticed it.

keyTerms.meaning: Son of noblemen, an affectionate and respectful way of addressing someone
Passes his hands over his face, covering the eyes for concentration
Yoke

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for the custom of covering the eyes while saying the first פסוק of שמע.

phrases.english: He said to him: Son of noblemen,
at the time that he passes his hands over his face,
he accepts upon himself the yoke of the Kingship of Heaven.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Rav's question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי said the first פסוק quietly while covering his face during his lesson.

steps.title: Did רבי later finish the rest of שמע?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether רבי went back later and completed the rest of שמע.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does he go back and finish it, or does he not go back and finish it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a new question about רבי's practice. This sets up the dispute in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We know that רבי said only the first פסוק during his lesson. The question is whether that was all he said, or whether he said the rest of שמע later.

keyTerms.meaning: Goes back and completes it

phrases.english: Does he go back and complete it,
or does he not go back and complete it?

steps.triggerLanguage: חוֹזֵר וְגוֹמְרָהּ, אוֹ אֵינוֹ חוֹזֵר וְגוֹמְרָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the fact that רבי said only one פסוק and asks what happened afterward.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Did רבי complete the rest of שמע at a later point?

steps.title: בר קפרא and רבי שמעון ברבי disagree
steps.stepSummary: בר קפרא says רבי did not finish שמע later. רבי שמעון ברבי, רבי's son, says he did.
steps.simpleTranslation: בר קפרא says: he does not go back and finish it. רבי שמעון ברבי says: he goes back and finishes it.
steps.whatsHappening: Two people close to רבי give opposite answers to the question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In בר קפרא's view, the one פסוק was רבי's entire שמע. In רבי שמעון's view, the one פסוק was only a quick acceptance of מלכות שמים, and רבי said the full שמע later.

keyTerms.meaning: A student of רבי
רבי שמעון, the son of רבי יהודה הנשיא

phrases.english: Bar Kappara says:
He does not go back and complete it.
Rabbi Shimon son of Rebbi says:
He goes back and completes it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives two opposing answers to the question in Step 29.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There is a dispute over whether רבי completed שמע later.

steps.title: Why did רבי look for a topic mentioning יציאת מצרים?
steps.stepSummary: בר קפרא challenges רבי שמעון: if רבי said all of שמע later, why did he make a point of teaching a topic that mentions יציאת מצרים?
steps.simpleTranslation: בר קפרא said to רבי שמעון ברבי: It makes sense according to me, since I say he does not finish it later. That is why רבי looks for a lesson that mentions יציאת מצרים. But according to you, who says he finishes it later, why does he need to look for such a lesson?
steps.whatsHappening: בר קפרא uses a known habit of רבי to attack רבי שמעון's position.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The third פרשה of שמע fulfills the מצוה to mention יציאת מצרים. If רבי never said that פרשה, it makes sense that he needed a lesson about the Exodus to make up for it. If he did say it later, the special search for such a topic seems pointless.

keyTerms.meaning: It makes sense according to me
Searches for, seeks out
A lesson or topic of learning
The Exodus from Egypt

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ בַּר קַפָּרָא לְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בְּרַבִּי:
phrases.english: Bar Kappara said to Rabbi Shimon son of Rebbi:
It works well according to me,
since I say 'he does not go back and complete it,'
that is why Rebbi seeks out a lesson
that contains the Exodus from Egypt.
But according to you,
who say he goes back and completes it,
why does he need to seek it out?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבי שמעון's side of the dispute.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי שמעון ברבי's claim that רבי completed שמע later.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Seeking out a lesson about יציאת מצרים only makes sense as a substitute for the third פרשה. If רבי said it later anyway, there would be no need for such a substitute.

steps.title: To mention the Exodus at its proper time
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון answers that רבי wanted to mention יציאת מצרים at its proper time, the time for קריאת שמע.
steps.simpleTranslation: In order to mention יציאת מצרים at its proper time.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון defends his view. רבי sought out the Exodus topic so that the mention would fall within the proper time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי may have said the full שמע later, possibly after the best time had passed. So he made sure to mention יציאת מצרים within its proper time through his lesson. The lesson was not a substitute for the third פרשה. It was a way to keep the timing of the mention correct.

keyTerms.meaning: To mention
At its proper time

steps.whatToRemember: רבי said only the first פסוק while covering his face during his lesson. בר קפרא and רבי שמעון ברבי argue whether he finished שמע later. Both agree he sought out a topic about יציאת מצרים. They disagree only about why: as a substitute for the third פרשה, or to keep the mention at its proper time.

phrases.english: In order to mention the Exodus from Egypt at its proper time.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers בר קפרא's challenge.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterprets the purpose of רבי's practice
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Seeking out the Exodus topic was a substitute for skipping the third פרשה.
steps.terutzMaskana: It was meant to keep the mention of יציאת מצרים within its proper time, even though רבי completed שמע later.

steps.title: Saying the first פסוק and then falling asleep is enough
steps.stepSummary: רבי אילא, in the name of רב, rules that someone who said the first פסוק of שמע and was then overcome by sleep has fulfilled his obligation.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אילא, son of רב שמואל בר מרתא, said in the name of רב: If someone said 'שמע ישראל ה' אלהינו ה' אחד' and then sleep overpowered him, he has fulfilled his obligation.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ruling: if you said just the first פסוק of שמע and then could not stay awake, you have still fulfilled the מצוה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This follows from the earlier steps, where רבי said only the first פסוק as קבלת עול מלכות שמים. The first פסוק is the essential core of קריאת שמע. So when sleep forces a person to stop after it, he has done the main part of the מצוה.

keyTerms.meaning: was forced or overpowered (here, by sleep)
sleep
he has fulfilled his obligation
the first verse of שמע

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that the first פסוק of שמע is the heart of the מצוה. The rest of the section builds on this idea.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי אִילָא בְּרֵיהּ דְרַב שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר מָרְתָּא
phrases.english: Rabbi Ila, son of Rav Shmuel bar Marta, said
in the name of Rav:

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר ״שְׁמַע יִשְׂרָאֵל ה׳ אֱלֹהֵינוּ ה׳ אֶחָד״
phrases.english: If one said, 'Hear, Israel, the Lord is our God, the Lord is One'
and was overcome by sleep, he has fulfilled his obligation.
phrases.notes: He was not being careless. Sleep simply overpowered him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אִילָא בְּרֵיהּ דְרַב שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר מָרְתָּא מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְרַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on רבי's practice of saying only the first פסוק, and turns the idea into a general rule.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Saying the first פסוק of שמע before being overcome by sleep fulfills the obligation.

steps.title: רב נחמן tells his servant to wake him only for the first פסוק
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן instructs his servant דרו to trouble him to stay awake for the first פסוק, but not for anything after it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said to his servant דרו: For the first פסוק, bother me (to keep me awake). For more than that, do not bother me.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a real-life practice that supports the rule it just stated. רב נחמן only made sure he was awake for the first פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן was willing to be disturbed so that he would say the first פסוק. He did not want to be disturbed for the rest. This matches רב's ruling that the first פסוק is the essential part.

keyTerms.meaning: his servant
bother me / trouble me (to keep me awake)
more (than that)

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב נַחְמָן לְדָרוּ עַבְדֵּיהּ:
phrases.english: Rav Nachman said to Daru, his servant:
For the first verse, bother me (to stay awake),
beyond that, do not bother me.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב נַחְמָן לְדָרוּ עַבְדֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Illustrates and supports the ruling of step 33 through a real practice.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that the first פסוק alone is essential.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב נחמן's instruction to his servant דרו.

steps.title: רב יוסף asks how רבה used to act
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף asks רב יוסף, the son of רבה, what his father did about staying awake for שמע.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said to רב יוסף, the son of רבה: How did your father act?
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup question. The answer, in the next step, gives another example of the same practice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יוסף wants to know a great teacher's personal practice. A rabbi's own conduct counts as a source for הלכה.

keyTerms.meaning: your father
how
would do / would act

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב יוֹסֵף לְרַב יוֹסֵף בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַבָּה:
phrases.english: Rav Yosef said to Rav Yosef, son of Rabba:
Your father, how would he act?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a second supporting example after רב נחמן's practice.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What רבה's practice was regarding saying שמע when sleepy.

steps.title: רבה made an effort only for the first פסוק
steps.stepSummary: רבה's son answers that his father pushed himself to stay awake for the first פסוק, but did not push himself for the rest.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: For the first פסוק, he would push himself (to stay awake). For more than that, he would not push himself.
steps.whatsHappening: The son answers the question. רבה also treated only the first פסוק as something worth fighting sleep for.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the same practice as רב נחמן's, but here the person troubles himself instead of having a servant do it. Two great אמוראים acting this way strengthens רב's rule.

keyTerms.meaning: troubled himself / made an effort (to stay awake)

steps.whatToRemember: The first פסוק of שמע is the essential part. Several אמוראים pushed themselves to stay awake for it, but not for the rest.

phrases.english: He said to him:

phrases.aramaic: בִּפְסוּקָא קַמָּא הֲוָה קָא מְצַעַר נַפְשֵׁיהּ,
phrases.english: For the first verse he would exert himself (to stay awake),
beyond that, he would not exert himself.

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּפְסוּקָא קַמָּא הֲוָה קָא מְצַעַר נַפְשֵׁיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 35.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבה exerted himself to stay awake only for the first פסוק.

steps.title: Someone lying on his back may not say שמע
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף rules that a פרקדן (someone lying flat on his back) may not recite קריאת שמע.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: Someone lying on his back should not recite קריאת שמע.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic: what body position is acceptable for saying שמע. רב יוסף forbids saying it while lying flat on your back.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Lying face-up is not a respectful position for accepting עול מלכות שמים. This connects naturally to the previous discussion of saying שמע in bed.

keyTerms.meaning: one lying flat on his back, face up
the recitation of שמע

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:
One lying on his back may not recite Shema.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף: פְּרַקְדָּן, לֹא יִקְרָא קְרִיאַת שְׁמַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from how much of שמע to say before sleep to which position is allowed when saying it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A פרקדן may not recite קריאת שמע.

steps.title: Is sleeping on your back allowed? רבי יהושע בן לוי cursed it
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא infers from רב יוסף that only reciting is forbidden, so sleeping on one's back would seem fine. It then challenges this, because רבי יהושע בן לוי cursed anyone who sleeps that way.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is it only reciting that he may not do, but sleeping that way is fine? But רבי יהושע בן לוי cursed whoever sleeps on his back!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reads an implication into רב יוסף's words and then attacks that implication with a strong source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יוסף only forbade reciting, which suggests that merely lying on your back is acceptable. But רבי יהושע בן לוי treated sleeping on one's back as so bad that he cursed it. So how could רב יוסף imply that it is permitted?

keyTerms.meaning: to lie down / to sleep
it is fine / permitted
curses
on his back

steps.confusionAlert: רב יוסף never said that sleeping on your back is allowed. The גמרא is drawing that out by inference ("only reciting is forbidden?"), and then challenging the inference.

phrases.english: Is it only reciting that he may not do,
but to lie (sleep) that way is fine?
But Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi
cursed one who sleeps on his back!

steps.triggerLanguage: מִקְרָא הוּא דְּלָא לִיקְרֵי, הָא מִיגְנָא שַׁפִּיר דָּמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges an implication of רב יוסף's ruling.
steps.kashyaTarget: The implied permission to sleep on one's back in רב יוסף's ruling.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יהושע בן לוי cursed sleeping on one's back, so it cannot be permitted.

steps.title: Leaning slightly: fine for sleeping, but not for saying שמע
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that lying on one's back while tilted slightly to the side is fine for sleeping. Reciting שמע is forbidden even when tilted.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said: To lie down while leaning slightly to the side is fine. But to recite, even if he is leaning, is still forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the challenge by describing a middle position, tilted slightly to the side, and giving it different rules for sleeping and for saying שמע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהושע בן לוי cursed sleeping fully flat on one's back. רב יוסף's implied permission refers to sleeping while slightly tilted. Saying שמע requires more respect, so even the tilted position is not good enough for it.

keyTerms.meaning: they said (an anonymous answer)
leaning / tilted slightly to the side
forbidden

phrases.english: They said:
Lying down while leaning to the side is fine,

phrases.aramaic: מִקְרָא אַף עַל גַּב דְּמַצְלֵי נָמֵי — אָסוּר.
phrases.english: but reciting, even when leaning, is also forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרִי, מִיגְנָא כִּי מַצְלֵי — שַׁפִּיר דָּמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 38.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing cases: fully flat versus slightly tilted, and sleeping versus reciting.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought רב יוסף implied that sleeping fully flat on one's back is allowed.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only sleeping while tilted is allowed. Reciting שמע is forbidden even while tilted.

steps.title: But רבי יוחנן leaned and still said שמע
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the answer, because רבי יוחנן would lean slightly and recite שמע.
steps.simpleTranslation: But רבי יוחנן would lean slightly and recite (שמע)!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer it just gave by pointing to רבי יוחנן's own practice. The next step answers this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer had said that reciting שמע is forbidden even while leaning. Yet רבי יוחנן, a major authority, did exactly that. So the rule just stated seems to contradict a great sage's behavior.

keyTerms.meaning: recites

phrases.english: But Rabbi Yochanan would lean and recite!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the תירוץ of step 39.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that reciting שמע while leaning is forbidden.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יוחנן's own practice was to lean and recite, which seems to contradict that rule.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן was a special case because he was very heavy
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers the challenge from רבי יוחנן: he was heavy, so he could not easily recite any other way.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן is different, because he was a very heavy man.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 40. רבי יוחנן's practice does not prove that a regular person may recite שמע while lying back and tilted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule from step 39 stays in place: reciting שמע lying on one's back is forbidden even when tilted. רבי יוחנן was allowed only because his heavy body made sitting or standing difficult. So his practice is a personal exception, not the general rule.

keyTerms.meaning: It is different. Used to show that a case is an exception.
A heavy, fleshy person.

steps.whatToRemember: A פרקדן may not recite שמע, even tilted slightly. רבי יוחנן was an exception because of his physical condition.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan is different
because he was a heavy (corpulent) man.
phrases.notes: It was hard for him to read any other way.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge raised in step 40.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Personal exception: a special circumstance explains the case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יוחנן's practice shows that reciting while tilted is allowed for everyone.
steps.terutzMaskana: It was allowed only for him, because he was heavy.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה about greeting between paragraphs
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's ruling (the view of רבי מאיר) on greeting someone in the breaks of קריאת שמע.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'At the breaks between paragraphs, one may greet, etc.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic by quoting a line from the משנה. It is setting up a question about that line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The full line in the משנה is רבי מאיר's ruling. In the breaks between paragraphs, one may greet out of respect and may answer. In the middle of a paragraph, one may greet out of fear and may answer. The word 'וְכוּ׳' tells us to read the rest of that line.

keyTerms.meaning: The breaks between the paragraphs of קריאת שמע.
Greets first, i.e., asks about someone's welfare.
Etc. The rest of the quote is understood.

phrases.english: At the breaks between paragraphs, one may greet, etc.
phrases.notes: Quote from the משנה, the view of רבי מאיר.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: New topic. The גמרא returns to the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In the breaks one may greet out of respect and may answer (רבי מאיר).

steps.title: Answering a greeting: for what reason?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the משנה allows a person to answer a greeting in the breaks.
steps.simpleTranslation: He may 'answer', but for what reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what the word 'answer' (מֵשִׁיב) in the משנה means. It wants to know for what reason, or for whom, one may answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה gives a reason for greeting first (respect) but gives no reason for answering. The גמרא wants to know what extra permission the word 'answer' adds.

keyTerms.meaning: Answers or returns someone else's greeting.
Because of what? For what reason?

phrases.english: He may answer — because of what?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the meaning of the משנה line quoted in step 42.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What is the reason or scope behind the permission to answer a greeting in the breaks?

steps.title: It can't mean answering out of respect
steps.stepSummary: If answering were only out of respect, the משנה would not need to say it, since greeting first out of respect is already allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say he may answer out of respect: now that he may even greet first, do we need to be told that he may answer?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests one possible meaning and rejects it. 'Answer out of respect' would be obvious.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Greeting someone first is a bigger interruption than answering a greeting. If the משנה already allows greeting first out of respect, answering out of respect is clearly allowed too. So the word 'answer' must be teaching something new.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say. Introduces a possible reading that will be rejected.
Out of respect, e.g., for a teacher or an important person.
Is it necessary to say he may answer? (It is obvious.)

steps.confusionAlert: Remember the logic: greeting FIRST is the bigger deal. Answering is the smaller deal. If the bigger one is allowed, the smaller one obviously is too.

phrases.english: If you say: answering out of respect,
now, if he may even greet first,
is it necessary to say he may answer?!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִילֵּימָא מִפְּנֵי הַכָּבוֹד, הַשְׁתָּא מִשְׁאָל שָׁאֵיל, אַהְדּוֹרֵי מִבַּעְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the first possible answer to the question in step 43.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Reading 'answer' as 'answer out of respect' in the breaks.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: That reading would make the word 'answer' unnecessary.

steps.title: In the breaks, one may answer anyone
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes: greet first out of respect, but answer any person at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it means: he greets first out of respect, and he answers any person's greeting.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives its explanation of the word 'answer': in the breaks, one may answer anyone's greeting.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Answering is a smaller interruption, so it is allowed more broadly. A person may answer even an ordinary person, not only someone who deserves respect. Now the word 'answer' teaches something new.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather. Introduces the accepted explanation.
To any person, even someone ordinary.

phrases.english: Rather: he greets first out of respect,
and he answers a greeting to any person.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא: שׁוֹאֵל מִפְּנֵי הַכָּבוֹד, וּמֵשִׁיב שָׁלוֹם לְכָל אָדָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the accepted reading after rejecting the reading in step 44.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: In the breaks: greet first out of respect, and answer anyone.

steps.title: Now apply the same method to the next clause
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא turns to the next clause of the משנה: in the middle of a paragraph, one greets out of fear and may answer.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now say the next clause: 'And in the middle, he greets out of fear and answers.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a challenge. It will apply the same question to the משנה's next clause.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The method that explained the first clause will now be used on the second clause. This leads to a problem, shown in the next steps.

keyTerms.meaning: Say the latter clause (the next part of the משנה).
The middle of a paragraph.
Out of fear, e.g., of someone who might harm him.

phrases.english: Say the latter clause:
'And in the middle, he greets out of fear, and answers.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the method from steps 43-45 onto the next clause of the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The method of reading 'answer' in the משנה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Applying the same method to the next clause will make רבי מאיר identical to רבי יהודה.

steps.title: In the middle, answering for what reason?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks the same question about answering in the middle of a paragraph.
steps.simpleTranslation: He may 'answer' in the middle, but for what reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks the same question it asked in step 43, now about the middle of a paragraph.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Again, the reason for greeting first is given (fear), but no reason is given for answering. The גמרא wants to know what extra permission the word 'answer' adds here.

phrases.english: He may answer — because of what?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the clause quoted in step 46.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What is the reason behind answering in the middle of a paragraph?

steps.title: It can't mean answering out of fear
steps.stepSummary: Answering out of fear would be obvious, since greeting first out of fear is already allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say he may answer out of fear: now that he may even greet first out of fear, do we need to be told that he may answer?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the reading 'answer out of fear', using the same logic as step 44.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If greeting first out of fear is allowed, answering out of fear is clearly allowed too. So the word 'answer' must allow something broader.

phrases.english: If you say: answering out of fear,
now, if he may even greet first,
is it necessary to say he may answer?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִילֵּימָא מִפְּנֵי הַיִּרְאָה, הַשְׁתָּא מִשְׁאַל שָׁאֵיל, אַהְדּוֹרֵי מִבַּעְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the first possible answer to the question in step 47.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Reading 'answer' as 'answer out of fear' in the middle of a paragraph.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: That reading would make the word 'answer' unnecessary.

steps.title: In the middle, one may answer out of respect
steps.stepSummary: In the middle of a paragraph, one may answer even someone who only deserves respect.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it means he may answer out of respect.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that in the middle of a paragraph, one may also answer a person who deserves respect.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Greeting first in the middle is allowed only out of fear. Answering, the smaller interruption, is allowed even out of respect. This follows the same pattern as step 45.

phrases.english: Rather: he answers out of respect.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the accepted reading after rejecting the reading in step 48.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: In the middle: greet first out of fear, and answer out of respect.

steps.title: Then רבי מאיר says the same thing as רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: With these readings, רבי מאיר matches רבי יהודה's ruling word for word. So what is their argument about?
steps.simpleTranslation: But that is exactly רבי יהודה's view! As we learned: רבי יהודה says, in the middle he greets out of fear and answers out of respect. In the breaks he greets out of respect and answers anyone's greeting. So what is the difference?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out a problem. Its explanations of רבי מאיר make him say exactly what רבי יהודה says in the משנה, but the משנה presents them as two different opinions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 45 (breaks: answer anyone) and step 49 (middle: answer out of respect) match רבי יהודה's ruling exactly. If both תנאים say the same thing, the משנה would have no reason to list them as two opinions. So the גמרא's reading needs to be fixed.

keyTerms.meaning: That is the same as. Used to point out that two views are identical.
As we learned in a משנה.

steps.whatToRemember: Under the גמרא's readings, רבי מאיר equals רבי יהודה. That is the problem the גמרא now needs to solve.
steps.whyThisMatters: A basic rule of learning a משנה: two named opinions should not say the identical thing. Spotting this forces the גמרא to find the real difference between them.

phrases.english: That is the same as Rabbi Yehuda's view!
As we learned: Rabbi Yehuda says:
In the middle, he greets out of fear
and answers out of respect;
and at the breaks, he greets out of respect
and answers a greeting to any person?
phrases.notes: Implied question: so what are רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה arguing about?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the challenge that step 46 began setting up.
steps.kashyaTarget: The readings of רבי מאיר given in steps 45 and 49.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Those readings make רבי מאיר identical to רבי יהודה, so the משנה's two opinions would have nothing to argue about.

steps.title: The משנה is missing words: רבי מאיר's full view
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says the משנה is incomplete and restores רבי מאיר's view. Answering is allowed only at the same level as greeting: respect between paragraphs, fear in the middle.
steps.simpleTranslation: Something is missing from the משנה, and this is what it really teaches: Between the paragraphs, a person may greet someone out of respect, and of course he may answer someone out of respect. In the middle of a paragraph, he may greet someone out of fear, and of course he may answer someone out of fear. These are the words of רבי מאיר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from Step 50 by saying the משנה is missing some words. It then fills in רבי מאיר's full opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before this, the גמרא read the משנה as saying that answering is allowed for a wider group than greeting. On that reading, רבי מאיר agreed with רבי יהודה. Now the גמרא reads 'אין צריך לומר שהוא משיב' as limiting answering to the same level as greeting. So in the middle of a paragraph, רבי מאיר allows answering only out of fear, not out of respect.

keyTerms.meaning: 'It is surely missing something.' The משנה's wording is incomplete and needs words added.
'And this is what it teaches.' The phrase that introduces the corrected reading.
'And needless to say.' Here it means answering is allowed at the same level as greeting, because answering is easier than greeting first.
'These are the words of רבי מאיר.' It marks whose opinion this is.

steps.confusionAlert: Do not read 'אין צריך לומר שהוא משיב' as 'he may answer anyone.' It means he may answer at the same level he may greet, and no further. That limit is exactly what makes רבי מאיר different from רבי יהודה.

phrases.english: The text is missing something,
and this is what it teaches:
At the breaks between paragraphs, one greets out of respect,
phrases.notes: Greeting first a person who deserves honor.

phrases.english: and needless to say, he may answer (out of respect).
phrases.notes: Answering is at the same level as greeting.

phrases.english: And in the middle of a paragraph, one greets out of fear,
and needless to say, he may answer (out of fear),
phrases.notes: Only out of fear, not out of respect.

phrases.english: these are the words of Rabbi Meir.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 50, which said רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה had become identical.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Correcting the text (חסורי מחסרא). Words are added to the משנה so that it reads differently.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The גמרא first thought that, according to רבי מאיר, answering covers a wider group than greeting. That made him the same as רבי יהודה.
steps.terutzMaskana: According to רבי מאיר, answering is allowed only at the same level as greeting. In the middle of a paragraph, that means only out of fear.
steps.whyThisMatters: This correction brings back the real argument in the משנה. It also shows that 'אין צריך לומר' sets the same limit for answering as for greeting.

steps.title: The corrected משנה: רבי יהודה's view
steps.stepSummary: Continuing the corrected text, רבי יהודה rules that in the middle of a paragraph one greets only out of fear but may answer even out of respect.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: In the middle of a paragraph, a person may greet someone out of fear, and he may answer someone even out of respect.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues reading the corrected משנה and now gives רבי יהודה's opinion. This shows where he disagrees with רבי מאיר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both of them agree that greeting in the middle of a paragraph is allowed only out of fear. They disagree about answering. רבי מאיר allows it only out of fear, while רבי יהודה allows it even out of respect. So the argument from Step 50 is now clear again.

keyTerms.meaning: Greeting someone first because you fear him, for example a powerful person.
Answering someone who greeted you because he deserves honor, even though you do not fear him.

steps.whatToRemember: In the middle of a paragraph, both רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה allow greeting only out of fear. רבי מאיר also limits answering to fear. רבי יהודה allows answering even out of respect.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:
In the middle of a paragraph, one greets out of fear
and answers out of respect,
phrases.notes: This goes further than רבי מאיר. The corrected text continues on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same corrected reading begun in Step 51, now giving רבי יהודה's side.
steps.terutzMaskana: In the middle of a paragraph, רבי יהודה allows answering out of respect, while רבי מאיר allows it only out of fear. That is the argument.
